claims.reason: S1 directly defines checkpointing as transferring WAL transactions into the database.
S3 states the post-commit frame threshold trigger. The disabling case is separately stated in f3; connection-local configuration is not explained here.
S3 explicitly makes non-positive N disable automatic checkpoints.
S3 gives the new-connection default, its page units, and its compile-time override.
S1 explicitly assigns PASSIVE to both listed checkpoint initiation mechanisms.
S3 supports the callback replacement interaction. This states only one direction of the rubric's reciprocal replacement rule.
S3 supports hook registration disabling configured autocheckpointing. This is the reverse interaction, not a duplicate of f6, but does not state both directions.
S1 specifies the active-reader end-mark boundary and its consequence for checkpoint progress.
S1 specifies both the saved progress location and continuation mechanism. It does not explain WAL-index lookup acceleration or host restrictions.
S1 explicitly connects continuous reader overlap to checkpoint starvation and unbounded WAL growth.
S1 identifies reader-free intervals combined with checkpoint attempts as a remedy for starvation.
S1 distinguishes normal WAL reuse from truncation and names the journal_size_limit exception.
S1 explicitly prohibits WAL reset during an ongoing write transaction.
S1 specifies WAL synchronization before database writes. This states only the first part of the rubric's synchronization sequence.
S1 specifies database synchronization before WAL reset. This states only the second part of the rubric's synchronization sequence.
S1 identifies the threshold-crossing COMMIT thread as the checkpoint executor. The latency consequence is not stated here.
S1 directly attributes slower triggering commits to checkpoint execution under the default scheduling strategy.

S2 supports both assertions, but nonwaiting frame processing and conditional database synchronization are separate operational rules. The claim does not explicitly state the complete PASSIVE rubric item.
S2 explicitly excludes busy-handler invocation in PASSIVE mode. The claim text omits possible incompletion, although its quotation includes it.
S2 supports the writer and reader waiting conditions and busy-handler qualification. Continued admission of new readers is omitted.
S2 describes complete frame transfer followed by database synchronization after FULL's waiting conditions are met.
S2 specifies the asymmetric effect of pending FULL on new writers and readers. It omits the waiting conditions required by the complete FULL rubric item.
S2 supports RESTART's additional reader wait and the busy-handler exception. The next-writer consequence is omitted.
S2 supports the next-writer restart consequence. The claim refers to, but does not specify, the database-only reader condition.
S2 explicitly states this pending-RESTART concurrency policy. The attribution accurately limits the assertion despite S1's conflicting reader-blocking warning.
S2 defines TRUNCATE through RESTART and specifies zero-byte truncation immediately before successful return.
S2 explicitly combines zero checkpointed frames with retrieval of pnLog and pnCkpt status.
S2 supports the exclusive checkpoint lock and SQLITE_BUSY on competing checkpoint contention. Busy-handler bypass is omitted.
S2 explicitly excludes busy-handler invocation for checkpoint-lock contention. The SQLITE_BUSY result is omitted.
S2 assigns the additional exclusive writer lock to exactly these three modes.
S2 specifies both busy-handler refusal points and the resulting PASSIVE fallback. The SQLITE_BUSY result is omitted.
S2 supports SQLITE_BUSY and possible incompletion after handler termination. This claim does not itself specify PASSIVE fallback or the affected modes.
S2 supports the frame count and failure sentinel for a non-null pnLog on a selected database. The combined pnLog/pnCkpt rubric item is only partially stated.
S2 explicitly defines pnCkpt as cumulative checkpointed frames, including earlier calls. The claim describes the count's meaning but omits its error sentinel.
S2 supports the null-or-empty selector and all-attached-WAL scope. Error-dependent continuation or abandonment is omitted.
S2 explicitly makes both output counters undefined when the operation selects all attached WAL databases.

f6–f7 establish reciprocal callback replacement effects beyond threshold configuration.
f8–f11 explain progress boundaries, resumption, starvation, and reader-gap mitigation.

f14–f15 establish the storage synchronization sequence.
f16–f17 connect default checkpoint execution placement with commit latency.
f18–f19 establish nonwaiting processing, conditional synchronization, and busy-handler exclusion.

f23–f25 establish an additional reader wait and the next-writer restart consequence.
f26 specifies a distinct successful-return guarantee of a zero-byte WAL; this is more specific than general recycling behavior.
f27 establishes a status-query operation that checkpoints no frames.
f28–f32 describe shared locking rules, contention failures, and fallback behavior across modes.
f33–f34 explain counter semantics, distinct from the NOOP operation used to retrieve them.
f35–f36 establish database selection and its effect on counter validity.
This broader parent is named but not developed as a separate technical idea by the claims; its full mechanism exceeds internal checkpointing scope.

overall_limitations: Several composite rubric facts are distributed across claims. Individual fragments receive no gold key unless they adequately state the complete rubric fact; this does not make those fragments unsupported.

Coverage omits fixed reader end marks, WAL-index lookup and host restrictions, the single-writer limit, explicit per-connection autocheckpoint configuration, attached-database error handling, NORMAL durability, and WAL-size-dependent read cost.
The packet contains conflicting reader-blocking descriptions for aggressive checkpoints. f25 accurately attributes its narrower statement to S2; the packet does not resolve the discrepancy.
All supplied sources share one documentation origin. No independent-origin requirement was supplied for this evaluation.
